contexts.text: From exercise they derive habit, and as it were nature. AC 1505.
Into the very habit of thus speaking come Souls immediately after death.
When it becomes of life, through habit it so imbues the man...
Habit from tarrying. Signified.
Everyone acquires for himself a nature Infrequent use and habit...
All evil which... by frequent use or habit has put on a resemblance of nature, is derived into the children... AC 8550.
What man does from the understanding, he at length does from the will, and finally by habit puts it on; and then it is insinuated into the rational or internal man.
When a man frequently does the truth, it then not only recurs from habit, but also from affection, and thereby from freedom.
(Thus) all things which enter with man remain; and the things which have derived a habit, that is, which have become familiar, are no longer apperceived to be in him.

They vanish out of the exterior memory, as is wont to be the case with the gestures, etc., and in general with the thoughts and affections... when by continual use or habit they become as it were spontaneous...
From custom (hypocrites) have contracted the habit of composing their interiors...
Hence from habit he contracts a moral and civil life in externals... and the effect of this habit is, that a man scarcely knows his own interiors...
If a man accustoms himself so to think, and from custom acquires a habit, he is then by degrees conjoined with Heaven.
That from his external habit no judgment can ever be formed in respect to the life of a man after death.
From habit in life can inspire others with such a persuasion.
They have contracted this from actuality and habit.
For from custom man contracts a habit and thus a nature.
I now perceive that this is a habit which is not good.
They contract the habit of speaking thus about others...
From custom it becomes... such a matter of habit...
As soon as there is actuality, it puts on custom, thus habit, and finally nature...
How it is that from habit or actuality such a result is produced... He derives from habit that they are familiar, so that he does not know he has them. SE 4226.
Actualities contract habit, and put on a species of nature. Example(s).
a. They frequented churches... merely on account of habit from infancy.
It is better still when he has contracted a habit, and begins to shun evil delights...
Mere external piety... is either hypocrisy, or somewhat feigned derived from habit...
